traceability.notes:
All acceptance criteria and requirements for 010.1-DEV-CONFIGURABLE-PATTERNS are fully implemented and verified.
Mapping to acceptance criteria:
1) Core Functionality (storyPathPattern / requirementIdPattern) - Implemented via the AnnotationRuleOptions interface in src/rules/helpers/valid-annotation-options.ts, which exposes both nested (`story.pattern`, `req.pattern`) and flat (`storyPathPattern`, `requirementIdPattern`) configuration fields. - valid-annotation-format.ts wires meta.schema = getRuleSchema(), so these options are part of the rule’s configuration surface. - Tests in tests/rules/valid-annotation-format.test.ts validate both nested and flat use: - Nested: [REQ-CONFIGURABLE-PATTERNS-STORY], [REQ-CONFIGURABLE-PATTERNS-REQ], [REQ-CONFIGURABLE-PATTERNS-BOTH]. - Flat: [REQ-CONFIGURABLE-PATTERNS-STORY-FLAT], [REQ-CONFIGURABLE-PATTERNS-REQ-FLAT], [REQ-CONFIGURABLE-PATTERNS-BOTH-FLAT].
2) Backward Compatibility - Default behavior is preserved by getDefaultStoryPattern(), getDefaultStoryExample(), getDefaultReqPattern(), getDefaultReqExample() and the initial resolvedDefaults. - resolvePattern returns the defaultPattern whenever no pattern is configured or a configured pattern fails to compile. - normalizeUserOptions returns undefined when no valid object is supplied, so resolveOptions falls back cleanly to defaults. - Tests confirm this behavior: - [REQ-CONFIGURABLE-PATTERNS-FALLBACK] invalid storyPathPattern/requirementIdPattern falls back to default behavior while still applying standard validation and (for story) auto-fix. - [REQ-CONFIGURABLE-PATTERNS-FALLBACK-FLAT] same fallback behavior for flat storyPathPattern / requirementIdPattern.
3) Pattern Validation (valid regex enforcement) - resolvePattern wraps new RegExp(...) in a try/catch and routes failures through buildInvalidRegexError, accumulating stable, engine-independent messages in optionErrors. - valid-annotation-format.create reads getOptionErrors() and reports invalidRuleConfiguration diagnostics on the Program node with the collected details, satisfying REQ-REGEX-VALIDATION. - Tests explicitly assert these configuration errors: - [REQ-CONFIGURABLE-PATTERNS-FALLBACK] (nested story.pattern and req.pattern) and [REQ-CONFIGURABLE-PATTERNS-FALLBACK-FLAT] (flat storyPathPattern and requirementIdPattern) expect an invalidRuleConfiguration error alongside standard format errors.
4) Error Messages (storyPathExample / requirementIdExample) - resolveExample prefers nested `story.example`/`req.example`, then flat `storyPathExample`/`requirementIdExample`, finally falling back to the defaults, satisfying REQ-EXAMPLE-MESSAGES and REQ-BACKWARD-COMPAT. - Tests verify examples appear and precedence is correct: - [REQ-CONFIGURABLE-PATTERNS-EXAMPLES] custom story/requirement examples appear in invalidStoryFormat/invalidReqFormat messages. - [REQ-PATTERN-CONFIG] and [REQ-EXAMPLE-MESSAGES] verify that nested *.example values override flat storyPathExample/requirementIdExample in error messages.
5) Quality Standards / Schema Validation - getRuleSchema returns a JSON-schema array with a single object schema containing: - nested story/req objects (pattern, example) with additionalProperties: false. - flat fields: storyPathPattern, storyPathExample, requirementIdPattern, requirementIdExample, autoFix. - valid-annotation-format meta.schema uses this schema directly, aligning with ESLint best practices and satisfying REQ-SCHEMA-VALIDATION.
6) Integration with valid-story-reference (storyDirectories) - valid-annotation-format focuses strictly on syntactic/regex validation of annotation values; it does not perform filesystem checks or directory resolution. - valid-story-reference (tested in tests/rules/valid-story-reference.test.ts) owns storyDirectories, allowAbsolutePaths, and requireStoryExtension semantics; its tests pass alongside valid-annotation-format’s configurable-pattern tests, demonstrating that pattern configuration does not interfere with path-resolution behavior. - API documentation clearly separates concerns: valid-annotation-format handles format/patterns, while valid-story-reference handles directory and file existence, satisfying the story’s integration intent (REQ-CONSISTENCY).
7) Documentation examples - user-docs/api-reference.md’s traceability/valid-annotation-format section documents exactly the options introduced by this story: - Nested story/req pattern and example options. - Flat shorthand options storyPathPattern, storyPathExample, requirementIdPattern, requirementIdExample. - Behavior notes about invalid patterns causing configuration errors and defaults being used when options are omitted. - It explains how to customize patterns to match different directory layouts and requirement ID schemes, corresponding to the story’s example use cases (different directory structures, different requirement prefixes, custom story file formats). This fulfils the “Documentation” acceptance criterion.
8) Direct requirement coverage - src/rules/helpers/valid-annotation-options.ts is explicitly annotated with: - REQ-PATTERN-CONFIG, REQ-REGEX-VALIDATION, REQ-BACKWARD-COMPAT, REQ-EXAMPLE-MESSAGES, REQ-SCHEMA-VALIDATION via @story docs/stories/010.1-DEV-CONFIGURABLE-PATTERNS.story.md. - src/rules/valid-annotation-format.ts meta.messages.invalidRuleConfiguration and create.Program handler are annotated with REQ-REGEX-VALIDATION and REQ-BACKWARD-COMP. - tests/rules/valid-annotation-format.test.ts includes a JSDoc header referencing docs/stories/010.1-DEV-CONFIGURABLE-PATTERNS.story.md and requirement IDs that align with the story’s intent (configurable patterns, examples, fallback behavior).
Given unchanged story requirements, passing tests (including all configurable-pattern and example-related cases), concrete implementation of options, validation, schema, and documentation, this story is fully implemented and passes.
